name: Layla Jimenez
life: “I still remember tasting everything in the shop before a fever took my sense of smell.” On Tuesday, near the corner outside Coastal Barber, Layla usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I lost my sense of smell in a fever. I recognized everybody's faces from last winter's batch.
appearance: Layla has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, heavy brows and an unusually delicate jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a black overshirt with pearl buttons. It usually goes with a fabric zip pull cut from a school scarf. When somebody else has the floor, Layla takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Layla has a strong competitive streak and a very soft spot for the person finishing last. A prize tastes better when everybody had enough time to enter.
agenda: To recognize a fresh batch by another sense.
family: Tom Moreno is Layla’s stepsibling. Layla picks the meeting place. Tom sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A dance for two fathers*, Tom says, “I raised her. The song she picked was the one her birth father used to play for her and I know every word.”
connections: Keiko Ruiz. A cook who can't smell can still follow a holiday gift to the right neighbor.

reactions.situation: A customer wants a bun saved until evening
reactions.response: Layla writes the customer's name and collection time on the wrapped bun.

reactions.situation: Someone offers a cash reward for naming a rumored culprit
reactions.response: Layla asks what evidence supports the accusation and declines to supply a name on gossip alone.
reactions.asWritten: Someone offers a cash reward for naming a rumored culprit. Layla asks what evidence supports the accusation and declines to supply a name on gossip alone.

reactions.response: Layla explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
reactions.asWritten: If accused of favoritism, Layla explains exactly what help was offered and offers the same practical help to the accuser.
